pr_title: Produce detailed diagnostic objects when test run assertions fail
pr_body:
<!--

Describe in detail the changes you are proposing, and the rationale.

See the contributing guide:

https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md

-->

<!--

Link all GitHub issues fixed by this PR, and add references to prior
related PRs.

-->

Fixes #34428

This PR tries to address some of the issues related to test assertion outputs

- The object references in the LHS and RHS expression condition of a run assertion will now be shown in full, instead of the compacted message that was being displayed.
- When a complex object has a marked (sensitive or ephemeral) value, the object will be show in full, with only the marked values redacted. e.g
```
  28:     condition = output.foo == var.foo[0]
    ├────────────────
    │ --- actual
    │ +++ expected
    │   {
    │     "field1": "value1",
    │ -   "field2": "value2",
    │ +   "field2": "different",
    │     "field3": "value3",
    │     "field4": "value4"
    │   }
```

- A diff representation for conditions (LHS (actual) - RHS (expected)) that are a result of binary operations, i.e `a == b`
- For objects of the different types, a statement is added to indicate the reason, because such objects may have the same visual json representation in the terminal. e.g {foo: null} vs {"foo": tonumber(null)}
- Tip: Please look through the tests in `test_test.go` file to see variaous output changes.

## Target Release

release, or as a patch to the current minor version. If you need to
port a security fix to an older release, highlight this here by listing
all targeted releases.

If targeting the next patch release, also add the relevant x.y-backport
label to enable the backport bot.

-->

pr_comments:
This is great!

Only feedback from me is that having _both_ the LHS / RHS _and_ diff output could be verbose in some situations? I  have run into cases where diffs are hard to parse in test output, but one thought would be maybe to set it so that the diff only is shown unless a verbose or debug flag is passed?

One thing I also find really helpful in other test frameworks is when the diff part shows explicitly what's expected and what's actual? Even though it's usually `-` for expected and `+` for actual, sometimes it's still a helpful reminder.
Maybe something like
```diff
--- expected
+++ actual
-   "bar": "notbaz",
+   "bar": "baz",
-   "qux": "(sensitive value)",
+   "qux": "quux",
```
I find the `|` on the left a little distracting, but I realize it's probably the terraform standard for errors?

> Only feedback from me is that having _both_ the LHS / RHS _and_ diff output could be verbose in some situations? I have run into cases where diffs are hard to parse in test output, but one thought would be maybe to set it so that the diff only is shown unless a verbose or debug flag is passed?

Thanks for the feedback @wyardley!. I like the idea of the LHS/RHS being in the verbose mode. I had planned to also move individual references (i.e var.foo[var.bar] are 2 references) into the verbose mode, and I'll move the values as well.

> --- expected
> +++ actual
> -   "bar": "notbaz",
> +   "bar": "baz",
> -   "qux": "(sensitive value)",
> +   "qux": "quux",

That's great feedback. Thank you. Also reminds me that we may want to colorize the outputs.


> I find the `|` on the left a little distracting, but I realize it's probably the terraform standard for errors?

That's right. The format precedes this change, so I think I will leave it be.
I didn't read the code too carefully, but how do the colors work? looks like there are colors applied, but mainly the same one? Do you have a screenshot of how the diff looks in a terminal?
Here is a screenshot example of the colorized output. It mimics similar style used in diffs for terraform operations
Nice! This looks great. This is truly going to be so helpful when working on tests.

Side note - I know it looks just like I posted above; but looking at it again, I’d more often expect it to work like a unified diff with the grouping like this. That might be complicated to do without using a third party lib, especially if you had a matching line in between.
But maybe:

```diff
--- expected
+++ actual
-   "bar": "notbaz",
-   "qux": "(sensitive value)",
+   "bar": "baz",
+   "qux": "quux",
```
and in the case where there’s a matching line in between, maybe like 
```diff
--- expected
+++ actual
-   "bar": "notbaz",
+   "bar": "baz",
    “matches”: “matches”,
-   "qux": "(sensitive value)",
+   "qux": "quux",
```
Of course, including some of the matching context like in that case might require some decision making in terms of how much overall context to show (like if you had 40 matching lines in between two non-matching ones). You could include a cut with 3-4 lines of matching context showing but again, maybe hard to implement.

Not sure what the sorting behavior is like or how commas should behave - I guess it depends how deep comparison of objects works? I think there’s still some complexity with comparison of objects without converting to JSON first.

issue_context.title: Produce more detailed diagnostics from failing test conditions
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version

```shell
v1.6
```


### Use Cases

The run condition expressions used in tests are going to primarily rely on equality for comparisons, and usually only between 2 values. When the values consist of complex types, the error diagnostics attempt to simplify the output by summarizing the references in the expression, like `is object with 4 attributes`, or `is tuple with 3 elements`. This summary doesn't usually help in the context of a test failure, since the types should be known, and the user is concerned with why the exact values in the expression aren't matching.

### Attempted Solutions

It is possible to break down the expression into multiple assertions, but it would be convenient to enable direct comparison of more complex objects.

### Proposal

Extend the diagnostic format for test failures, which can print complete values or even create smart diffs based on those values in the UI.

### References

#34425
comments: This will be very useful, I just face this scenario it was very hard to know what the issue was :(

review_comments:
Just a heads up- when I was originally looking into marking test diagnostics as explicitly due to an assertion failure I discussed this implementation with Liam and a sticking point was naming. The pre-existing `DiagnosticCausedByEphemeral`, etc, makes it sound like the test failed _due to_ ephemerality but I think it's more accurate to say that there was an ephemeral in play when the diagnostic was raised.

In contrast, `DiagnosticCausedByTestFailure` is meant to convey a causal link between the test failure and the diagnostic.

There's nothing you need to change here, but I wanted to share that context!

Thanks for that context!

> The pre-existing DiagnosticCausedByEphemeral, etc, makes it sound like the test failed due to ephemerality but I think it's more accurate to say that there was an ephemeral in play when the diagnostic was raised.

You're absolutely right. This definitely make more sense. The original code was more of a workaround.

Regarding the interface implementations, they aren't currently utilized for failed assertions in `internal/command/views/json/diagnostic.go` where diagnostics are displayed in output. I've already created a separate path specifically for handling failed assertion diagnostics there.

I've however left the interface implementations in place as a forward-looking measure. If a future code starts analyzing diagnostics differently without special handling for failed assertions, they'll be available to serve that purpose.
